shared.surfBiteReport: Note: The most current report I was able to pull surf-specific content from for the PCB/30A Gulf-front stretch is approximately 3 weeks old (mid-July 2026), so treat this as recent but not this week's conditions. Along the beaches from Panama City Beach westward through the 30A corridor, the surf bite has been steady with Spanish mackerel, whiting, redfish, and jack crevalle showing up consistently — best action runs from first light to around 9 a.m. and again in the final hour or two before sunset, when baitfish push close to shore and predators follow. Water temperature is 85°F. Target the deeper cuts and troughs between sandbars rather than bombing casts to the horizon, as most surf species are feeding surprisingly close in; watch for diving birds or jumping bait to locate the action. Whiting are providing the most reliable numbers on sand fleas, shrimp, and Fishbites fished in the troughs, while Spanish mackerel respond well to spoons and small swimbaits retrieved quickly along the surface.
